predecessors.name: Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic
predecessors.text: the RSFSR, whose territory the Russian Federation inherited: 'On 25 December 1991, following the dissolution of the Soviet Union' (Russia page)

predecessors.name: Soviet Union
predecessors.text: the Soviet Union's seat, Moscow, and its continuing international role passed to the Russian Federation; no land beyond the RSFSR's

ledger.x: 1991: the Russian Federation emerges from the Soviet Union.
1992: the Transnistria War leaves Russian military presence on the Dniester.
11 December 1994: Russian troops enter Chechnya.
May 1995: Russian forces hold most of Chechnya.

31 August 1996: the Khasavyurt Accord ends the First Chechen War after separatist 'Operation Jihad' (6 August 1996) 'effectively reversing Russian gains'; it 'deferred the decision on Chechnya's status until 2001'.
End of 1996: Russian forces leave Chechnya.
October 1999: the second invasion of Chechnya.
2 February 2000: Grozny falls.
April 2000: the main phase ends and Chechnya is back under Russian rule.
30 April 2000: end of the main phase of the Second Chechen War; guerrilla fighting continues until the counter-terrorism regime ends on 16 April 2009 but holds no territory.
August 2008: Russia recognises and garrisons Abkhazia and South Ossetia.
8 August 2008: Russian forces invade Georgia's undisputed territory.
8 October 2008: Russian forces leave the buffer areas.
27 February 2014: Russian troops take Crimea.
February 2022 onward: Russia occupies the south of Ukraine.
24 February 2022: Russian forces cross into Kyiv, Chernihiv, Sumy and Zhytomyr oblasts.
26 February 2022 onward: Russian forces occupy the east of Kharkiv Oblast.
Late March - early April 2022: Russia withdraws from north of Kyiv.
September 2022: Ukraine's Kharkiv counteroffensive ends the occupation.
30 September 2022: Russia annexes the Luhansk People's Republic.
30 September 2022: Russia annexes the Donetsk People's Republic with its 2022 gains ('about 60% of Donetsk Oblast' held).
9-11 November 2022: Russia withdraws from Kherson and the right bank.
August 2024: Ukraine enters Kursk Oblast.

wars.name: First Chechen War
wars.outcome: Russia took most of Chechnya by May 1995 but lost the initiative in August 1996; the Khasavyurt Accord of 31 August 1996 deferred Chechnya's status to 2001 and federal forces withdrew by the end of 1996.

wars.name: Second Chechen War
wars.outcome: Russia reconquered Chechnya in the main phase (7 August 1999 - 30 April 2000), imposed direct rule in May 2000 and ended its counter-terrorism operation on 16 April 2009; the separatists were reduced to an insurgency.

wars.name: Russo-Ukrainian war
wars.outcome: Russia occupied Crimea in 2014 and, after the 24 February 2022 invasion, about 'roughly 20%' of Ukraine; it proclaimed the annexation of four oblasts on 30 September 2022; Ukraine retook Kharkiv Oblast (September 2022) and Kherson (11 November 2022).

wars.name: Russo-Georgian War
wars.outcome: Russia invaded Georgia's undisputed territory on 8 August 2008 ('1-16 August 2008' in the infobox; ceasefire negotiated by Sarkozy on 12 August); it occupied Zugdidi, Senaki, Poti and Gori and pulled back from the buffer areas on 8 October 2008; Georgia lost…

certainty.note: The post-Soviet frontiers follow the Soviet republic and oblast lines and later treaties.
